status: UNADOPTED AUTHORING PROPOSAL; UNSENT; all 31 GD questions

sharedProposal.acquisition: NEW full-feat proposal: use an actual legal class ASI/feat opportunity and check the printed prerequisite at acquisition. Level means total character level. Ability increases from these feats have the ordinary ceiling of 20 and do not grant another feat or ASI. For a feat with other benefits, a score already at or above the applicable ceiling gains zero from its +1 clause but does not lose points or make the other grants ineligible. The pure ASI option below separately requires a full legal allocation. Except the expressly repeatable Ability Score Improvement, Armor Proficiency and Resilient proposals below, each identity is nonrepeatable. Different names remain different identities. Later prerequisite loss does not retroactively revoke ownership; actual ongoing equipment/body/effect requirements still apply.
sharedProposal.capacityIsNotRecovery: RETAIN the already reviewed MAXIMUM_HP_PLAYTEST component contract: Tenacity uses current total level; Tough keeps twice acquisition-level snapshot; Tough as Nails uses two per acquisition level plus two for each later level; Dark Fortitude uses twice current total level. Distinct feat identities add; duplicates do not. Recompute from separate records. Capacity increases grant no current HP. Capacity decreases clamp current HP without damage, Wounds, healing or new first-fall triggers. These decisions are already reviewed components and are not reopened by full-feat authoring.
sharedProposal.abilityChanges: Apply a real permanent ability increase once and recompute its derived modifier. Recompute base maximum HP from stored attained-level values and current CON using the existing per-level floor, then the reviewed maximum-HP ledger. Do not refill current HP, Hit Dice, RP, RC, class pools or uses. Acquisition of a newly limited-use feat follows the NEW proposal of one initially available use unless its exact procedure says otherwise; this never refills another feature.
sharedProposal.timingAndRerolls: NEW common reroll completion: after an eligible failed saving throw but before its consequences commit, spend the feature's use and replace the complete original one- or two-d20 save procedure with the same applicable advantage/disadvantage and modifiers. Use the new result even if worse. The feature cannot reroll its own replacement. Other exact reroll features keep their own windows and costs; no committed consequence can be undone. A completed long rest refreshes short-rest uses under existing timing, while extra turns or calendar changes do not.
sharedProposal.damageAndHealing: Retain actual attack/save, passive defense, prevention, temporary HP, Core damage and life-state ordering. Resistance never stacks with another resistance of the same scope. Immunity remains immunity. Proposed paid reactions below specify their separate timing and cannot be invoked after damage has already committed. Ordinary healing follows current modifiers, prohibitions, finite funding and Critical ceiling; direct state recovery is expressly identified and receives no ordinary healing bonuses. Neither operation restores an actually dead creature without a genuine resurrection source.
sharedProposal.mentalPredicate: NEW proposed finite definition for Iron Will and Resilient Mind: a qualifying mental-effect save is the effect's own save to prevent or end Charmed, Frightened, possession, compelled actions/speech, or an explicitly described alteration of thoughts, memories, beliefs, emotions or perceived sensory reality; also include a save directly against psychic damage. Actual concentration maintenance is a separate save, not automatically a mental-effect save because psychic damage caused it. A generic INT/WIS/CHA save, mundane physical hazard or ordinary social check does not qualify solely by ability or theme. Tag the actual effect and outcome before the roll; this classification needs the full spell/class conference.
sharedProposal.limits: All new action costs, quantities, types, timing bridges and eligibility interpretations below are proposals requiring GPT discussion. Exact previously reviewed components remain carried. Source descriptions and legacy variants stay preserved, including inactive immunity/regeneration language. No creation of a curse, ancestry, plane, soul, origin or missing body profile is authorized. Human balance and complete feat runtime remain open.

proposals.procedure: Use one actual earned ASI/feat choice to increase one ability by 2 or two distinct abilities by 1 each. Retain the source description's ceiling of 20 for this feature. NEW: this entry is the registry representation of that ordinary ASI option and may be selected at each legitimate ASI opportunity; choosing it does not give both an ASI and another feat. The one-score option requires room for the full +2, and the two-score option requires room for both full +1 increases; do not waste or bank part of the award. Record the acquisition event and chosen scores, then recompute actual modifiers and other derived statistics under the shared rules. No current HP/resource refill, retroactive class selection, starting feat or extra ASI schedule is created. Use each class's real ASI levels, including Oracle's specific schedule, rather than total-level multiples.
proposals.newChoices: Registry ASI identity and repeatability; full legal increase allocation and no banking. Source ability-20 cap preserved.
workedCases: At one earned opportunity, STR 18 can become 20, or STR 19 and WIS 13 can become 20 and 14. That same opportunity cannot also acquire Tough.
A multiclass character reaching total level 4 without an actual class ASI milestone receives no new ASI merely from this registry entry.

proposals.procedure: Choose one actual armor proficiency tier: light, medium or heavy. Preserve the source's lack of a prerequisite: NEW explicit selection permits direct heavy-armor proficiency without first learning lighter tiers. Only the chosen tier is granted; heavy does not automatically grant light, medium, shields, weapons or tools. NEW repeatability: this feat may be acquired again through another actual feat choice for a different armor tier not already proficient; record each chosen tier under one source family with distinct acquisition events. Choosing an already proficient tier gives no benefit and is not an eligible new selection. Training does not supply armor, alter fit/anatomy, remove its Strength requirement, waive donning time or invent an AC bonus. While legally using the selected tier, remove only the nonproficiency consequences that actual proficiency removes; other properties remain.
proposals.newChoices: Direct tier choice retained; repeatability for distinct missing tiers only; no implied lower-tier/shield grants.
workedCases: An unarmored character can spend this proposed feat choice on heavy armor proficiency, but remains untrained in a separately used shield.
A second acquisition can select medium if it is genuinely missing. It cannot select heavy again to stack AC or obtain an unrelated skill.

proposals.procedure: Choose Strength or Dexterity and increase it by 1, normally no higher than 20. Climbing does not cost extra movement solely because it is climbing; terrain, crawling, squeezing and other independent costs remain. This grants no climbing Speed, handholds, ceiling adhesion, automatic check success or immunity to falls. For a running long jump, add your current Strength modifier in feet to the otherwise legal horizontal distance. NEW: the increase has a minimum of zero when that modifier is negative, and a running approach requires at least 10 feet of actual immediately preceding movement on support. The approach and jump both spend movement; clearance, checks and legal landing remain. This does not increase a high jump or ordinary standing long jump. Improved Athlete's separate proposal supplies its own standing-distance change and retains this running increase once. The approach and negative-modifier completions require the full movement-source decision before adoption.
proposals.newChoices: Score cap; no negative 'increase'; explicit 10-foot approach and movement-budget interpretation. No new climb mode.
workedCases: A legal running jump with baseline 16 feet and STR modifier +3 can span 19 feet, still paid from actual movement after its approach.
A character with STR modifier -1 gains no extra jump distance and suffers no extra one-foot reduction from this feat. Difficult terrain on a climb still costs its terrain surcharge.

proposals.procedure: Don or doff an actual suit of armor in half its normal time, preserving its real steps, access, hands, closures and fit. NEW: apply this factor once to the selected suit's existing armor duration; do not automatically include shields, weapons, jewelry or other gear. Combine the separately authorized single helper's doff-time halving multiplicatively with this feat because they represent distinct sources, then round elapsed time upward once to a whole second. In initiative, spend enough complete Actions/turn intervals to cover that elapsed work without compressing an Action below its legal availability; partial progress is retained only to the extent the armor procedure actually permits. Extra helpers do not further halve the time. Interruption leaves the real partially completed state and does not make the armor usable sooner. Gain advantage on each actual initiative roll; this creates neither a new roll after order is established nor an extra turn. Multiple initiative-advantage sources do not stack.
proposals.newChoices: Armor-only scope; actual helper composition and final-second rounding; initiative-event boundary.
workedCases: A normal 60-second armor doff becomes 30 seconds; one real helper can reduce it to 15 seconds under this proposed composition. Two helpers do not reduce it to 7.5 seconds.
A shield whose separate rule takes one Action still takes that Action; the feat does not convert it to a free interaction.
dependencies: Reviewed don/doff table and helper rule

proposals.procedure: NEW: as a Bonus Action, spend the feat's one long-rest use to enter this feat rage for one elapsed minute. Gain resistance to bludgeoning, piercing and slashing damage, whether magical or nonmagical, and add 2 damage on each actual successful melee attack you own. The melee scope includes weapon, unarmed, natural and melee spell attacks; it is not limited to weapons. Add the flat 2 once to the attack's primary damage type before target defenses; it is not doubled by a critical hit and is not a separate hit, copied damage or spellcasting trigger. NEW: the rage ends early if you voluntarily end it as a Bonus Action or become Incapacitated. It does not require attacking or taking damage to continue, prohibit spellcasting/concentration, extend through repeated attacks, or grant unstated class rage features. Another real rage may coexist under its own rules, but same-scope resistance does not stack and bonuses obey their actual families; this feat's flat rider cannot be counted twice under aliases. A completed rest restores the use, not an encounter declaration.
proposals.newChoices: Bonus Action activation/end, physical-type mapping, melee attack breadth, flat rider attribution and incapacity ending.
workedCases: A critical melee weapon hit doubles its actual damage dice but adds this feat's flat 2 only once. A separate ranged attack receives none of this rider.
An already bludgeoning-resistant holder remains resistant, not quarter-damage, when the rage begins. Becoming Stunned ends this proposed rage through Incapacitated.

proposals.procedure: Preserve the printed prerequisite exactly: Dragonborn, or a Sorcerer with an actual draconic bloodline. Neither name is silently replaced by Drakari or Mage. NEW mechanical eligibility record: identify an actual controlling character/lineage source that expressly establishes one of those prerequisites and its one draconic ancestry damage type. Without that evidence the feat is not selectable in the current candidate; the name alone is not a lineage grant. Once legitimately acquired, gain resistance to that recorded actual damage type and the source's ability to speak, read and write Draconic under the reviewed language procedure. The language grant does not supply writing tools, hands or current speech when an independent condition prevents it. Existing resistance does not stack, and an existing language grant does not produce a substitute language or feat. No bloodline, species origin, dragon allegiance or cosmology is authored here. Resolve any proposed legacy-name alias in the actual source conference before opening eligibility.
proposals.newChoices: Evidence-backed prerequisite/type record and duplicate-language handling; unmatched identity stays unresolved without inventing an alias.
workedCases: A Drakari entry with no explicit Dragonborn alias does not automatically satisfy the printed prerequisite. A verified historical alias would need to be recorded by the source decision first.
An actually eligible source specifying fire produces fire resistance and Draconic literacy/speech, not a free choice among every dragon damage type.

proposals.procedure: Increase Constitution by 1, normally no higher than 20, and recompute the real derived modifier and maximum-HP records without healing. For each actual Hit Die legally spent and rolled to restore HP, NEW: set that die's pre-healing-modifier amount to the greatest of its ordinary die-plus-CON healing amount, twice the current signed CON modifier, and zero. Apply the minimum after the ordinary die-plus-CON calculation, separately per die, before ordinary healing bonuses, reductions, blockers and maximum/Critical caps. The resulting actual HP gain may be less than this raw minimum or zero. It creates no Hit Die, rest permission or automatic restoration of spent dice. Wounds reduce actual Hit Dice recovery under their existing rule, not this individual die's result. Do not floor the die face itself at twice CON or multiply a combined multi-die pool a second time.
proposals.newChoices: Per-die floor after die-plus-CON, nonnegative bound and placement before ordinary healing pipeline.
workedCases: CON modifier +3 with a Hit Die face of 1 normally gives 4; Durable makes the raw healing 6 before actual healing modifiers and caps.
CON modifier -1 with a die face of 1 gives zero under the proposed floor, not negative healing. A genuine no-HP-gain effect can still prevent a positive Durable result.

proposals.procedure: Require Constitution 15 and an actual recorded source event satisfying the printed exposure-to-an-elemental-plane prerequisite. This record is a literal eligibility receipt, not permission to invent a plane or reinterpret an origin. NEW finite mechanical choice at acquisition: select acid, cold, fire, lightning or thunder as the feat's one permanent damage type; this menu is proposed, not a recovered elemental taxonomy. Gain resistance to that type. Your actual unarmed strikes replace their ordinary base damage type with the selected type; they do not add a second packet, new dice or another ability modifier. Other separately sourced riders keep their own types. Use actual unarmed attack proficiency, ability, action economy and body legality. A natural weapon is not automatically an unarmed strike unless its source says so. No creature-type change, anatomy, emitted aura, elemental immunity or automatic environmental protection is granted. A new type choice requires an explicit later retraining source; none is created here.
proposals.newChoices: Five-type operational menu and base unarmed-type replacement; exposure remains receipt-bound without new lore.
workedCases: Selecting lightning changes a legal unarmed strike's normal base damage to lightning. It does not add an extra lightning die on top of the old bludgeoning damage.
Without an actual qualifying exposure receipt, Constitution 15 alone does not unlock the feat or establish that a planar trip occurred.

proposals.procedure: NEW precise deprivation bridge: while this feat is operative, accrue only half the ordinary food-, water- and sleep-deprivation time toward each respective unmet-need deadline. Use the same elapsed world clock, preserving fractional accrued time and prior exposure; do not halve the actual daily food/water quantity. A nominal 24-hour no-water threshold therefore requires 48 actual hours of otherwise identical deprivation under the feat. Partial intake and resets follow the actual deprivation procedure. Acquisition does not erase already accrued debt or penalties, and suppression changes future accrual rather than replaying old time. Gain advantage on actual Constitution saves whose source prevents or resists gaining the Exhaustion condition. NEW: include a Constitution save against ordinary environmental expedition Strain only if the source explicitly equates that save with exhaustion; do not apply it to Dissonance, serum Strain or every similarly named track. Sleep tolerance gives no short/long-rest benefits, extra active-work Watch, free recovery or exemption from an actual hard work cap. The live expedition verdict must supply the final baseline schedules and distinct track mapping.
proposals.newChoices: Half-rate future deprivation accrual, no retroactive cure, exact save predicate and preserved rest/work limits.
workedCases: Twelve actual hours without water adds six hours to a deprivation clock that would ordinarily accrue one-for-one. It does not produce half a ration of missing water.
Remaining awake longer does not itself restore RP or grant a beneficial long rest. An unrelated Warrior serum-Strain save does not gain this feat's advantage by name alone.

proposals.procedure: The printed prerequisite is Charisma 13; acquiring this feat does not require or grant an Elf/Feykin ancestry. Gain advantage on actual saving throws to prevent or end the Charmed condition. NEW: qualify by the actual effect's Charmed outcome, not merely an Enchantment school or a persuasive theme; no new save is created for a no-save effect. Prevent a new magical application whose actual source puts you to sleep. This does not block ordinary sleep, fatigue, zero-HP Unconsciousness or a magical effect that causes Unconsciousness without sleep. NEW prospective boundary: acquiring or unsuppressing the feat does not itself end an already applied sleep effect; that effect retains its own wake/removal rules unless it explicitly checks immunity continuously. A new sleep application while protection is operative fails. Other independent damage/conditions from the same source remain. This feat grants no creature type, lineage history, charm immunity or fear immunity.
proposals.newChoices: Charmed/sleep predicates and prospective sleep protection; no implicit ancestry gate or origin claim.
workedCases: An eligible Charisma-13 character of a different ancestry can acquire the feat through a legal choice and gains its mechanical protections without becoming Feykin.
A spell that newly puts the holder to sleep is prevented. Falling to zero HP from ordinary damage still follows Core Unconsciousness and death rules.

proposals.procedure: After computing the current body's ordinary physical carrying capacity and inventory Load capacity from actual Strength and size, double both capacities. NEW: the same factor also doubles the corresponding push/drag/lift limit so that the paired physical-handling limits remain coherent. It does not double an item's weight, remove carried cargo, alter casualty Load, enlarge a mount's capacity or multiply an already modified result twice. Distinct capacity effects use their actual stacking clauses; no generic repeated doubling is granted. You may wield a weapon made for a body one size category larger than your actual current body without a size-only handling penalty. Use that weapon's actual reviewed item profile, hands, reach, damage and properties; the feat itself adds no damage die, reach, proficiency, free hand or two-size permission. An oversized weapon without a complete source profile remains an item-authoring dependency rather than receiving improvised bigger statistics. Real anatomy and Strength requirements still apply.
proposals.newChoices: Pounds/Load/push-drag-lift capacity binding and one-category weapon permission; no invented oversized profile.
workedCases: A Medium STR-18 body has ordinary 270-pound carry and 18 Load; this proposal gives 540 pounds and 36 Load, with the corresponding lift/push/drag limit doubled once.
Wielding an actual Large weapon does not give a Medium holder Large reach or an extra damage die unless that weapon's complete profile expressly supplies it.

proposals.procedure: Gain resistance to cold damage. NEW explicit type mapping: treat the source's undefined 'heat damage' as fire damage for this feat, granting fire resistance rather than introducing another damage type. This mapping requires joint approval; a different typed effect does not qualify merely because its narration sounds hot. Gain advantage on actual saving throws directly against poison or disease, including a permitted save to prevent or end that actual ailment. These protections do not stack with other resistance or advantage sources. They do not cure an existing illness, prevent the Poisoned condition without a save, erase a dose's non-save consequences or automatically defeat environmental heat/cold exposure that uses a separate save or deprivation rule. An ordinary exposure Constitution save is not a poison/disease save unless its real source says so.
proposals.newChoices: Heat-to-fire mapping and poison/disease save predicate; no generic environmental immunity.
workedCases: A 9-point fire component is reduced under ordinary fire-resistance rounding after its other applicable damage stages; a separately typed radiant component is unchanged.
A disease-recovery save can gain advantage. The feat does not automatically cure that disease or prevent starvation in a hot region.

proposals.procedure: NEW full healing procedure: as an Action, spend one real healer's-kit charge to treat one adjacent legally reachable living creature. Choose ordinary stabilization only, or this feat's healing treatment. A full actual kit has ten charges, costs 5 gp and weighs 3 lb under the reviewed item rule; transfer or partial use never refills it. Healing treatment has one entitlement per recipient per that recipient's completed short or long rest, shared across all Healer practitioners. Commit that entitlement and the charge before resolution even if healing is later blocked. If the recipient is dying, first cause an actual dying-to-Stable transition using this paid kit use, then resolve ordinary healing of 2d4 plus the practitioner's signed Wisdom modifier, minimum zero before the normal healing pipeline. One charge funds both parts of this single treatment. If HP gain is blocked, the stabilization remains with its genuine recovery deadline; if positive HP returns, close that obsolete deadline normally. A recipient whose healing entitlement is spent may still receive ordinary kit stabilization for its real charge and Action, without more feat HP. Already Stable creatures can receive the once-per-rest healing but create no new stabilization trigger. This removes no Wounds, Injury, disease or death. Independently owned Field Medic/Field Surgeon triggers require their actual source/event and own limits, with no duplicated kit charge or invented second stabilization.
proposals.newChoices: Action, one-charge cost, 2d4+WIS healing, recipient short-rest family cap, blocked-offer commitment and stabilization-before-healing sequence.
workedCases: One charge treats a dying target: record stabilization, then dice 3+2 and WIS +3 give 8 ordinary healing before actual modifiers/caps. A second Healer owner cannot repeat the HP treatment before that target rests.
Under a broad HP-gain prohibition the target remains Stable at zero; the charge and healing entitlement are spent. The feat does not resurrect a dead body.
dependencies: Reviewed kit, stabilization and healing pipeline

proposals.procedure: Require actual medium-armor proficiency at acquisition. Gain heavy-armor proficiency and increase Strength by 1, normally no higher than 20. NEW: record the actual Strength increase at acquisition, including zero if already at the ceiling; another existing heavy-proficiency grant produces no substitute skill, shield, feat or Expertise. Later loss of a prerequisite does not erase ownership, but actual suit/body legality continues to apply. Heavy proficiency removes only the relevant nonproficiency penalties while using that armor; it does not supply the suit, grant medium/light/shield proficiency a second time, change AC formula, waive Strength minimum, eliminate Stealth disadvantage, cancel weight/Load or shorten donning. A source suppressing training operates under its own actual duration without undoing the permanent score history.
proposals.newChoices: Score cap, duplicate-grant handling and acquisition-time prerequisite; no armor-property waiver.
workedCases: A medium-trained character with STR 15 can become STR 16 and learn heavy armor through one legal feat choice; a real suit still has to be acquired and donned.
Already knowing heavy armor yields no extra proficiency, though the actual permitted +1 Strength remains the feat's separate benefit.

proposals.procedure: Require Constitution 17 and total character level 10. From acquisition onward, accrue natural biological aging at half the body's otherwise applicable natural rate. NEW: keep elapsed world time and accumulated age separate; the feat does not reverse existing age or halve a discrete magical aging event unless that event expressly changes the natural aging rate. Suppression restores future ordinary accrual without retroactive catch-up or rejuvenation. This is a bounded mechanical clock, not immortality, resurrection or a new lifespan/cosmology claim. Gain advantage on actual death saving throws at the existing regular-turn start. Roll the two dice and select the higher before resolving death-save natural 1/20 and counters. Ordinary advantage cancellation applies. No extra death save occurs on an extra turn, and the feat does not replace Instant Death, a fatal Wound save, an effect without a death save or an already dead state.
proposals.newChoices: Future natural-aging accrual versus discrete magical events; death-save advantage integration without new saves.
workedCases: Two elapsed years under an unchanged ordinary aging rate add one biological year, while the world calendar still advances two years.
Death-save faces 1 and 12 select 12 under advantage, giving the ordinary success. The feat does not permit a roll after actual Instant Death.
dependencies: Actual age records; no new lifespan lore

proposals.procedure: Add 2 once to the actual saving throw against a mental effect meeting the shared proposed finite predicate. This can apply to an INT, WIS, CHA, CON or other save if the actual effect qualifies; it is not a blanket ability-based bonus. The same source cannot add twice when one effect both causes fear and deals psychic damage. No bonus applies to an opposed skill check, death save, ordinary concentration maintenance or an effect granting no save. NEW stacking completion: this distinct feat bonus can combine with Resilient Mind's independently applicable +1 Wisdom-save rider, subject to any explicit overriding source restriction; class-technique bonuses first obey their own strongest-only family. Preserve actual natural-save rules and any printed failure margin. The feat supplies no immunity, automatic success, new save, changed belief or agency override.
proposals.newChoices: Shared mental predicate and explicit distinct-feat combination with Resilient Mind; existing +2 retained.
workedCases: An actual Wisdom save against Charmed can receive Iron Will +2 and an owned Resilient Mind's qualifying +1, for a proposed total +3 from those distinct feats.
A Constitution concentration save caused by psychic damage is not itself the attack's mental-effect save; Iron Will does not add +2 merely from that causal history.

proposals.procedure: Gain light-armor proficiency and shield proficiency, preserving both printed grants despite the feat's name. Choose Strength or Dexterity and increase that score by 1, normally no higher than 20. Existing proficiency in either category provides no unprinted substitute training or Expertise; the other actual grants still apply. NEW: treat this as one nonrepeatable feat identity with the chosen score recorded at acquisition. Training does not give armor or a shield, free a hand, grant two shields' AC, waive fit, auto-don equipment or add an AC modifier beyond the actual item's reviewed contribution. Shield proficiency removes its own relevant nonproficiency consequences; light-armor proficiency applies only to that armor tier. Recompute actual derived statistics without healing or refilling resources.
proposals.newChoices: Score cap and fixed duplicate-grant handling; source light-plus-shields breadth retained.
workedCases: A character already proficient in shields can still gain light armor and the legal +1 chosen ability; duplicate shield training does not become another skill.
A shield's real hand/forearm occupancy and donning Action remain. The feat's name is not grounds to omit its explicit shield proficiency.

proposals.procedure: Require medium-armor proficiency at acquisition. While wearing an actual medium suit, remove only that suit's Stealth-disadvantage cause; other remaining causes still combine normally with advantage. When the selected operative AC formula is that medium suit's formula and your current Dexterity score is at least 16, raise its Dexterity contribution cap from 2 to 3. Use the actual Dexterity modifier, including any penalty, capped at 3; this is not a flat +3 added to AC. If Dexterity falls below 16, use the ordinary cap of 2. A shield's legal bonus remains separate, and another chosen unarmored/natural formula gains nothing from this medium-suit modification. NEW: a Broken or otherwise nonbeneficial suit supplies no positive AC formula benefit, although removing that suit's Stealth-disadvantage cause still applies while it is physically worn. Other properties, weight, Strength limits and actual fit remain.
proposals.newChoices: Live DEX threshold, formula-specific cap and Broken-suit treatment; no broad Stealth advantage.
workedCases: A medium suit with base AC 14 and DEX 16 contributes 14+3=17 before a real shield. DEX 14 uses 14+2=16.
Removing the suit's Stealth disadvantage does not remove an unrelated Exhaustion disadvantage or grant automatic Hidden.
dependencies: Reviewed AC formula and Broken equipment rules

proposals.procedure: At total character level 6 or higher, once per completed short rest, after failing an actual saving throw to prevent or end Frightened or another source explicitly designated as a fear effect, you may spend this feat's use to reroll under the shared save-replacement procedure. Keep the new result. A no-save fear effect supplies no eligible roll, and success does not cure unrelated conditions. NEW operative-source choice: use the current reroll effect; preserve the description/legacy fear-immunity wording as an inactive alternative rather than granting both. Advantage/disadvantage applies to the replacement as it did to the original complete save procedure. A failed replacement still applies the original effect's actual failure outcome; it is not an automatic success. No additional Action or Reaction cost is proposed because this is a response within the original save's uncommitted result window.
proposals.newChoices: Current effect controls over legacy immunity; fear predicate and complete-procedure reroll timing.
workedCases: After a failed advantaged fear save, spend the one use and roll the replacement two-d20 procedure. Its new failed result must stand if still below the actual DC.
A fear aura with no saving throw cannot be canceled by inventing a Mental Fortress save. The feat grants no immunity under this proposed current-effect selection.

proposals.procedure: Require actual light-armor proficiency at acquisition. Gain medium-armor and shield proficiency, and choose Strength or Dexterity to increase by 1, normally no higher than 20. Preserve all three printed benefits. NEW: one nonrepeatable identity records the actual chosen score and grants; already held medium/shield proficiency gives no substitute selection or Expertise. The feat does not waive suit properties, body fit, Strength minimum, weight, don/doff time or hand use. Apply the actual selected armor formula and shield contribution, with the ordinary cap unless a separately owned feature changes it. Later loss of the acquisition prerequisite does not erase ownership; ongoing item/body restrictions and actual suppression still govern use.
proposals.newChoices: Score cap, nonrepeatability and duplicate-training handling; no hidden lower/upper-tier grants.
workedCases: A light-trained holder with DEX 15 can become DEX 16 and gain medium armor plus shields. The medium suit still uses its normal +2 DEX cap without Medium Armor Master.
Existing shield proficiency does not create an extra skill when this feat is acquired; the medium training and legal ability increase remain.

proposals.procedure: Preserve the current effect: when you legally spend one or more Hit Dice during a completed short-rest recovery procedure, add your current PB once to the total ordinary HP-healing amount for that rest. NEW: commit this single Quick-Recovery-family addition with the first actual Hit Die healing event of that rest; further installments or extra dice in the same rest do not add it again. Zero spent Hit Dice yields no feat addition. Add PB before the ordinary healing reductions, prohibitions and capacity/Critical caps; it is not a promise of PB actual HP restored. The entitlement is spent even if that first event is blocked or entirely excess, and a separate owned converter still needs its own actual rules. Wounds affect recovered Hit Dice under their existing procedure, not a second fee on this bonus. The description/legacy +50-percent out-of-combat regeneration remains preserved but inactive. No free recurring regeneration, extra rest reward or new Hit Dice is created.
proposals.newChoices: Once-per-real-rest total bonus, first-event commitment and inactive legacy regeneration choice.
workedCases: PB +3 with two Hit Die results totaling 11 gives 14 raw ordinary healing for that rest, before actual healing modifiers and caps; spending another die later in the same rest adds no second +3.
A rest spent without any Hit Die gives no Quick Recovery healing. A blocked first Hit Die heal does not reserve the bonus for repeated retries.

proposals.procedure: Choose one of STR, DEX, CON, INT, WIS or CHA. Increase that score by 1, normally no higher than 20, and gain proficiency in saving throws using that same ability. NEW repeatability: a later actual feat opportunity can select a different ability, but cannot select the same ability again through this feat. Record the chosen ability and acquisition event; there is no free switch or banked +1. An existing save proficiency adds no second PB or Expertise, though an otherwise legal +1 ability remains. Check the score ceiling for each selection. Apply the actual save ability only when that save is made, including other legitimate modifiers; proficiency is not a bonus to every save. Recompute derived statistics and the CON/maximum-HP records where relevant without ordinary healing or resource refills.
proposals.newChoices: Different-ability repeatability, score cap and duplicate-save handling; same ability binds both benefits.
workedCases: Selecting WIS 15 makes WIS 16 and grants Wisdom-save proficiency. A later separate selection may choose CON, but not WIS again.
If Wisdom saves were already proficient, selecting a legal WIS increase does not add PB twice or grant Expertise on those saves.

proposals.procedure: Add 2 on actual Constitution saving throws whose purpose is maintaining concentration on a real active effect. This does not create concentration on an effect that lacks it, grant a new slot or add to every Constitution save. Separately add 1 on actual Wisdom saves against a mental effect under the shared proposed finite predicate. The two clauses have different roll requirements and do not both apply to one ordinary Constitution concentration save. Preserve the current source's save wording over its legacy 'concentration checks' shorthand; an effect using a different non-save procedure is not automatically converted. NEW: its distinct qualifying Wisdom +1 can coexist with Iron Will's +2 under the proposed feat-family rule. No effect without an actual save grants an invented roll, and no bonus automatically prevents concentration ending from Incapacitated, voluntary replacement or its source's dependency ending.
proposals.newChoices: Separate exact predicates, current-save wording and explicit Iron Will combination.
workedCases: A CON concentration save with ordinary modifier +4 becomes +6. Its causal psychic damage does not also activate this feat's Wisdom-only +1.
A qualifying WIS save against mental coercion can receive the +1, while an unrelated Wisdom-based navigation check receives nothing.

proposals.procedure: Once per completed long rest, after you fail an actual saving throw whose currently applicable failure outcome directly makes you Dead, you may spend the feat's use to reroll under the shared replacement procedure before death commits. NEW eligible examples include an explicit save-or-die effect and a Wound save begun at three Wounds, where another failure is immediately fatal. An ordinary damage save does not qualify merely because the eventual damage could reduce HP to zero or meet Instant Death; that save's failure outcome is damage, not direct death. Ordinary death saving throws and their accumulated failure counters are a separate Core procedure and do not qualify here. No-save direct death, an already committed death, a maximum-HP clamp or a future delayed risk supplies no new save. Use the new result even if it still kills; there is no resurrection or automatic survival. Preserve legacy death-effect 'resistance' wording as inactive beside this explicit current reroll proposal. A separately eligible would-die replacement still keeps its own later legal window if the new result remains fatal.
proposals.newChoices: Exact direct-death failure predicate; fatal Wound inclusion; damage/death-save exclusions; precommit reroll timing.
workedCases: At three Wounds, a failed actual Wound save would kill. This proposal permits one paid reroll before committing that death, with the new save's actual result controlling.
A failed fire-damage save is not eligible merely because the incoming damage is lethal. A no-save Instant Death check supplies no Stubborn Resolve roll.

proposals.procedure: At total character level 4 or higher, acquire Tenacity through a legal feat opportunity. RETAIN its reviewed maximum-HP component: one bonus record equal to your current total character level, including already attained levels. It updates with genuine later level changes; do not snapshot it at acquisition. It is one identity and cannot be counted twice through aliases, engine descriptions or repeated registration. Distinct Tough, Tough as Nails and Dark Fortitude records add under the already reviewed maximum-HP contract. Apply systemic factors and reductions in that contract's order. Gaining or restoring this bonus increases capacity only; losing/suppressing it recomputes capacity and clamps current HP if necessary without damage, Wounds, healing, death-failure or first-fall triggers. NEW full-feat completion: nonrepeatable acquisition and retention under ordinary later prerequisite loss; no free retraining or HP refill.
proposals.newChoices: Only full-feat acquisition/nonrepeatability completion; existing HP coefficient, stacking and no-healing rule are retained authority.
workedCases: At total level 7, Tenacity contributes +7 maximum HP. A later genuine level 8 makes that +8 without restoring a missing current HP point.
With current HP 35 and maximum 40, removing a +7 Tenacity record can clamp HP to the recomputed maximum 33; the two-point clamp is not damage.

proposals.procedure: Acquire Tough through one legal feat opportunity and record total character level at that moment. RETAIN the reviewed component decision: its maximum-HP bonus is twice that acquisition-level snapshot, with no automatic later increment from Tough itself. Keep that snapshot through current level changes, temporary suppression and save loading; do not rewrite it to current level or borrow Tough as Nails' later-level clause. Distinct maximum-HP feat identities add under the reviewed ledger, but duplicate Tough copies do not. Capacity increases give no current HP; removal/suppression can clamp current HP without damage or healing triggers. NEW full-feat completion: nonrepeatable, with no ordinary re-acquisition loop to replace the snapshot at a higher level. Only a separately authorized actual retraining/removal procedure could create a genuinely new acquisition event; this feat supplies none.
proposals.newChoices: Nonrepeatable acquisition and no snapshot-reset loop; reviewed snapshot/stacking component stays unchanged.
workedCases: Tough acquired at level 4 contributes +8 even after the character reaches level 10. Tough as Nails' separately owned later-level rule does not rewrite this record.
Suppressing and restoring Tough keeps the original +8 snapshot and restores no current HP.

proposals.procedure: Require total character level 5 at acquisition. RETAIN the reviewed maximum-HP component: +2 for each total character level already gained, and +2 for each genuine later gained level. Record acquisition level and each subsequent actual advancement so that the benefit tracks the actual attained-level history without replaying level events. NEW edge completion: if a separately authorized level-loss rule removes a level and its benefits, remove the corresponding later-level +2 contribution; restoration of that same level restores that contribution once, not an additional duplicate. The ordinary candidate currently grants no free level loss/retraining mechanism. Preserve source description/legacy +10-percent wording as an inactive alternative, not a second bonus. Distinct HP feat identities add under the already reviewed ledger. Capacity changes never heal and clamps are not damage. This feat is nonrepeatable.
proposals.newChoices: Full-feat gate/nonrepeatability and explicit replay-safe level-loss edge; reviewed current coefficient and legacy distinction retained.
workedCases: Acquiring at level 5 gives +10 maximum HP; reaching level 6 adds exactly +2, for +12. It does not also apply the legacy +10 percent.
Replaying the saved level-6 advancement event adds nothing after that same event is already recorded.

proposals.procedure: Gain resistance to necrotic damage. You can see normally through magical darkness with your current functioning visual sense. NEW precise scope: within the range at which that body's normal vision can resolve a subject under adequate light, treat magical darkness's obscuring effect as absent for your sight; where the magic itself creates a dark region, treat that region as normally lit for this personal perception. This emits no light and grants no benefit to allies. Independent ordinary darkness beyond that region, non-darkness fog/smoke, total cover, invisible creatures, lack of eyes, Blinded and an actual vision-range limit still apply. It neither creates a new visual sense in a sightless form nor extends a specified sense range. Existing necrotic resistance does not stack. The name/descriptive void connection grants no planar origin, alignment change, creature type or other cosmological assertion.
proposals.newChoices: Personal normally-lit interpretation for magical darkness, actual visual-range/body boundary and no light emission; no invented fixed range.
workedCases: A visible unobstructed target inside magical darkness can be seen by a holder with functioning ordinary sight. An invisible target remains invisible without another exact ability.
A wall still blocks sight and a sightless form gains no eyes from this feat; necrotic resistance remains its separate benefit where otherwise operative.

proposals.procedure: Require Constitution 13 and total character level 6 at acquisition. For the two damage defenses, the holder must currently have an actual operative transformation or an explicitly recorded lycanthropic curse. A cosmetic disguise, feat name or inferred origin is insufficient. Gain resistance to nonmagical slashing damage and halve an actual silver weapon's own damage components, including any intrinsic item-profile components. Separate poison doses, class/feat riders and spell damage are not silver-weapon damage merely because the weapon hit delivered their trigger, unless an exact source says they are part of that weapon's own damage. NEW: the two passive halves supplied by this same feat form one defensive family; a nonmagical silver slashing hit is halved once by this family, not automatically quartered. Resolve separate actually applicable defenses by the governing damage pipeline. Gain advantage on actual saves to resist an involuntary transformation, without creating a save for a no-save change. Once per completed long rest, when a real positive-to-zero HP transition would occur while actually transformed, you may spend the use to remain at 1 HP instead. NEW: this is a true drop-prevention floor after Instant Death checking and before later Wound consequences; it does not override Instant Death, fatal Wounds, an already-zero state, actual death or a mandatory unpreventable cost. Extend only the current transformation's ordinary time endpoint, if needed, to at least the end of your next original regular turn. It does not shorten a longer duration, create another form, waive upkeep, prevent voluntary ending or preserve a form through independently failed concentration, invalid anatomy, suppression or another mandatory source ending. Keep the source's origin/curse language as a literal eligibility receipt without inventing a curse.
proposals.newChoices: Actual form/curse predicates; same-feat passive-halving family; true-floor order and limited time-endpoint extension. Silver-weapon native components are explicitly separated from independent riders.
workedCases: An eligible nonmagical silver slashing packet of 11 is halved once by this feat's own passive family, yielding 5 before any other distinct legally ordered stage, not 2 from counting both clauses twice.
A transformed positive-HP holder can spend the floor use on an eligible drop, but a subsequent failed Wound save begun at three Wounds can still kill under Core. The feat is not resurrection.

proposals.procedure: Gain advantage on actual saves against poison and disease. RETAIN the reviewed maximum-HP record of +2 per current total character level, additive with distinct HP feat identities and never a current-HP refill. RETAIN its continuous strict-below-half threshold: poison resistance applies exactly while 2 × current HP is less than effective maximum HP. Freeze eligibility for a damage component at its actual defense evaluation; later HP loss does not retroactively resist earlier damage in that packet. Once per completed short rest, when a positive necrotic damage component is about to reach you after passive defenses and before temporary HP/normal HP, NEW: spend your available Reaction and this feat use to halve that remaining necrotic component, rounding the remaining amount down. Other damage types in the same event are unchanged. This is a separate paid prevention step and can follow an actual passive necrotic resistance, but never double-apply either stage or replay a committed packet. You must legally be able to react at that window; zero-HP Incapacitated supplies no generic permission. Necrotic Affinity's separate reaction remains its own choice/cost and does not activate for free from this feat. No prevented amount becomes healing or temporary HP here.
proposals.newChoices: Exact paid reaction window, necrotic-component halving/rounding and no generated resource; reviewed HP/threshold components retained.
workedCases: With effective maximum 21, HP 10 is strictly below half and grants poison resistance; HP 11 does not. A later maximum change recomputes the continuous predicate without a damage event.
A remaining necrotic component of 5 can be reduced to 2 by the paid Reaction. A simultaneous 4 fire remains 4; no temporary HP is granted.
dependencies: Reviewed maximum HP and strict thresholds

proposals.procedure: Require Constitution 15 and actually owned Necrotic Affinity or Dark Fortitude, using their exact feat IDs. Gain resistance to necrotic and poison damage. NEW delayed-recovery procedure: once per completed long rest, after an actual positive-to-zero damage/loss event finishes its Core Instant Death, Wound and death processing and leaves you living at zero, you may commit the use to that real dying/Stable episode. Record a recovery deadline at the start of your next original regular turn, preserving its virtual marker if initiative changes. At that deadline, before the normal death save, if you are still living at zero in that same episode, attempt direct state recovery to 1 HP. Broad HP-gain prohibition blocks the point; it does not create stability or refund the use. Earlier positive healing closes the pending episode and cancels this later recovery without reducing HP; actual death cancels it and cannot be reversed. On actual successful recovery, NEW: gain a one-elapsed-minute rider adding 2 necrotic damage once to each genuine personally owned damaging attack/spell/feature event, before target defenses. Apply it once to a shared area roll/event, with each target resolving its own defenses; a mixed-type packet does not gain it per component. Fixed damage and actual ongoing source ticks can qualify, but copied/reflected damage, another creature's actions and newly invented split packets do not. The flat +2 is not doubled by critical hits. It is this feat's damage component, not ordinary spell damage for Lifeleech, and creates no new spell, hit, payment, resource event or damage root; it cannot recursively trigger itself. Direct recovery does not remove Wounds, Prone or an independent cause of Unconsciousness. It ends on its deadline or your actual death and does not stack with itself. Missing this delayed recovery or being killed before it never becomes a later corpse wake-up.
proposals.newChoices: Episode-bound regular-start recovery, before-death-save placement, blocked/early-healed/dead branches and exact one-minute +2 necrotic rider scope. Distinguish direct recovery from resurrection.
workedCases: The holder drops to zero and survives the packet, commits the use, then receives ordinary healing before the next regular start. That real episode closes; the delayed effect neither lowers them to 1 HP nor grants its recovery rider.
If still alive at zero at the deadline, legal direct recovery restores 1 HP before the death save and starts the minute-long rider. If already dead, neither recovery nor rider occurs.
